Subject: Post-call: SDK handoff + throttling & idempotency checklist

Hi Sarah, Tom — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can get the technical handoff moving: 

Recap
- Primary integration lanes: web backend (Go) + a small Python microservice for ranking.
- Expected baseline: ~120 req/s, with bursts to ~300 for 30–60s.
- Latency target: P95 < 300ms for generation endpoints, reranker can be higher.

Attachments
- I attached an "SaaSCo-Integration-Checklist.pdf" that has the suggested SDK steps and checklist.
- Also attaching a small text file with idempotency header examples.

Immediate asks for you (Sarah):
1) Confirm SDK languages (Go/Python) and whether you want us to push a sample repo.
2) Confirm whether you prefer API keys (short-term) vs. JWT client auth (long-term).
3) Provide any procurement/contract contact so we can route pricing questions.

Our proposed plan (high level) — we want to validate these in a 30-minute technical handoff with your team and our engineers: 
- Auth: API keys + optional per-service JWT in Private deployments.
- Routing: route requests by model profile (latency vs. cost) with automatic fallback to cached or smaller model.
- Structured output/tool calling: use function-schema v2 for deterministic parsing + tool fallback for external calls.
- Embeddings/reranker: hybrid flow — ANN search (embedding store) to retrieve candidates, cross-encoder rerank on top N.
- Throttles & retries: client token-bucket + server quotas; standard exponential backoff with jitter on 429s; use idempotency keys for mutating ops.

If that sounds good I'll schedule the handoff and loop in Aditya and Neha to cover SDK and infra specifics.

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — that recap is helpful. A few quick answers: 
- Languages: yes, Go for backend, Python for the ML ranking service. We may also have a Node.js edge lambda in front of the backend later.
- Auth: we'll start with API keys for the POC. Long-term we'd prefer a JWT-based approach so we can rotate per-service creds.
- Procurement: looping in Tom for contract/procurement details (tom.nguyen@saasco.com).

Two important constraints from our side: 
1) We have strict burst detection in our platform and cannot accept silent queuing beyond 60s — if you return 429s we need clear guidance on backoff and whether to route to a cheaper / cached response.
2) For ranking, we prefer to keep candidate retrieval deterministic and use a cross-encoder reranker to preserve high precision on top-5.

Also attaching our internal security checklist (see Drive link in thread) and a short doc on expected SLAs. We'll confirm times for the handoff in a follow-up.

—Sarah

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@saasco.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@saasco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jul 2028 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK handoff + throttling & idempotency checklist

Great notes, Sarah — appreciate the constraints. Below is a proposed concrete plan addressing the two items and the broader integration: 

1) Throttling & Quotas (what to implement) - Client-side: leaky-bucket / token-bucket limiter in SDKs (we can provide Go + Python libs). Configure default tokens/sec = 150 with burst capacity = 300 for 60s windows. - Server-side: per-API-key quota that enforces minute and daily caps; returns 429 + "Retry-After" header. - Fallback strategy: on 429, SDK should (a) check cached response for similar request (if applicable), (b) if none, optionally downgrade to a cheaper model (e.g., small-llm variant) and return a degrade flag in response metadata.

2) Retries & Idempotency - Retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter. Example: base=500ms, multiplier=2, max_retries=5. Stop retrying on 401/403/4xx except 429. - Idempotency: require client to send X-Request-ID (UUID v4) for any non-idempotent operation (requests that change server state or do billing-sensitive calls). Server stores recent ids with a TTL (suggest 24–48h) and returns HTTP 409 if a duplicate conflicting request arrives. - Logging & tracing: propagate request id to Redwood tracing and include in user-visible error payload for debugging.

3) Routing & Structured Output - Routing: use route policy by model tag (e.g., "low-latency", "high-quality"). We'll include automatic fallback mapping in case preferred model is overloaded. - Structured output/tool calling: recommend function-schema v2 and strict validation in SDKs. For external tool calls, return a "tool_call" object in the response with canonical fields (tool_name, inputs, confidence).

4) Embeddings & Reranker - Retrieval: ANN store (Faiss/HNSW) with normalized vectors; fetch top 100 candidates via embeddings. - Reranker: cross-encoder re-rank top 8–16 candidates. Reranker should run at a higher latency budget and be independently autoscaled.

Next steps - I'll upload sample idempotency code to the shared Drive and Marissa will prepare SDK install instructions. - Can we do a 30-minute tech handoff Tuesday? (Aditya to lead SDK topics, Neha to cover security/compliance).

Attaching: sample-idempotency-snippets.txt (header examples + small pseudo-code).

Thanks,
Rishi

Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK handoff + throttling & idempotency checklist

Looping in some implementation-level notes from infra/SDK: 

- Retry algorithm: 
  * base_delay = 500ms
  * multiplier = 2
  * max_delay = 8s
  * max_attempts = 4 (we've found diminishing returns after 3-4 retries for user-facing requests)
  * jitter = uniform(0, base * pow(multiplier, attempt)) (full jitter)

- Idempotency storage: use Redis with dedupe keys: idempotency:<api_key>:<request_id> storing a small serialized response +/- TTL 24h. For high-volume keys, use a size-bound eviction and log collisions.

- 429 handling: honor Retry-After when present. If Retry-After > 10s, recommend immediate fallback to cached response or trigger degraded path (smaller model). For bursty traffic, autoscaler policy should add capacity up to a configured soft-limit before shedding.

- Reranker infra: keep the cross-encoder on a separate pool. Use continuous batching (up to 8 examples) and KV cache for hot inputs. This keeps P95 low while preserving quality.

- Structured output: SDKs will expose a validation helper that ensures the function schema matches the declared tool signature before invoking. Fail fast on mismatch.

I can prepare a short demo snippet (Go + Python) showing X-Request-ID usage, retry wrapper, and fallback wiring.

—Aditya
